Joint Headline HICP — 4-component Bayesian VAR with SV and model-based outliers¶

This is the current production Headline model.

The model is intentionally simple and joint:

[ y_t = \begin{pmatrix} \Delta\log HICP^{Energy}_t\\ \Delta\log HICP^{Food}_t\\ \Delta\log HICP^{NEIG}_t\\ \Delta\log HICP^{Services}_t \end{pmatrix}. ]

All four components are endogenous in one monthly BVAR. This removes the need to pair posterior draws from separately estimated component models and gives a single joint posterior distribution for the four Headline blocks.

The detailed WP374 component models are deferred decomposition models and live under notebooks/decomposition/. They are not required to run this notebook.

Production choices¶

  • canonical model: dense BVAR(12);
  • only lag sensitivity: dense BVAR(6);
  • no sparse-lag restriction in the joint model (active_lags=None);
  • same validated Energy-suite Bayesian machinery:
    • Minnesota shrinkage;
    • stochastic volatility;
    • model-based outliers;
    • Durbin–Koopman ragged-edge treatment;
    • shared registry/diagnostics.

The four model inputs are aggregate HICP indices. Therefore every variable uses the same transformation:

[ HICP_t \rightarrow \log(HICP_t) \rightarrow \Delta\log(HICP_t). ]

The Food aggregate is read from Haver ticker H023HA1@EUDATA. Annual Food aggregation weights are constructed upstream as Processed Food + Unprocessed Food official HICP weights.

def find_project_root(start: Path) -> Path:
    start = start.resolve()
    for candidate in (start, *start.parents):
        if (candidate / "data").exists() and (candidate / "src").exists():
            return candidate
    raise FileNotFoundError("Could not locate project root containing data/ and src/.")

Variable ordering¶

The canonical order is fixed as:

1. HICP Energy
2. HICP Food
3. HICP NEIG
4. HICP Services

The BVAR forecast itself is the primary object. Any future recursive structural interpretation must explicitly acknowledge this ordering; this notebook does not label the recursive innovations as economic structural shocks.

Every equation is estimated on monthly log changes:

[ 100\Delta\log(HICP_t). ]

The factor 100 above is only for human-readable plots. The shared model engine receives log(HICP) state levels and internally takes the ordinary first difference.

5. Historical bottom-up Headline reconstruction¶

Before estimating the BVAR, validate the aggregation contract using observed data.

For calendar year (y):

[ I_t^{Headline}¶

I_{Dec(y-1)}^{Headline} \sum_i \frac{w_i^y}{1000} \frac{I_{i,t}}{I_{i,Dec(y-1)}}. ]

The first year is anchored to the official HICP Total in the previous December. The reconstruction then chains recursively across years.

This test is particularly important because the Food index comes from Haver while its annual weight is constructed from official Processed + Unprocessed Food weights. The index base itself is irrelevant to the ratio formula, but the historical reconstruction must still be economically coherent.

The historical reconstruction does not backfill annual weights. It starts automatically at the first year for which:

  1. all four annual component weights are available;
  2. all four component indices are observed in the preceding December;
  3. official HICP Total is available in that preceding December for the initial anchor.

Thus an earlier component-index history does not force the reconstruction to start before the official aggregation weights exist.

The joint BVAR has four endogenous variables. In the canonical BVAR(12), each equation has 48 lag coefficients before the constant, so Minnesota shrinkage is essential.

There is no automatic lag search. The methodology is fixed:

baseline    = dense BVAR(12)
sensitivity = dense BVAR(6)

    headline_forecast,
    official_total,
    kind="level",

    headline_forecast,
    official_total,
    kind="yoy",
)
display(fig)
plt.close(fig)

The annual-weight policy is explicit:

  • use the published weight vector for year (y) when available;
  • if the forecast horizon enters a future year whose weights are not yet published, carry forward the latest complete published vector;
  • never backfill a historical weight gap.

The aggregation is performed on component index paths, not on weighted inflation rates.

15. Only lag sensitivity: dense BVAR(6) versus dense BVAR(12)¶

No automatic lag-selection exercise is performed.

The sole robustness comparison is:

dense BVAR(12) — canonical baseline
vs
dense BVAR(6)  — sensitivity

The production baseline remains BVAR(12) unless the shorter model reveals a material stability or forecasting problem. A formal forecast-performance comparison should later use the same pseudo-out-of-sample evaluation window for both models.

In [ ]:
if RUN_BVAR6_SENSITIVITY:
    result_6 = run_headline_joint_bvar(
        native_levels,
        vintage=VINTAGE_USED,
        p=SENSITIVITY_P,
        prior_config=PRIOR_CONFIG,
        sampler_config=SAMPLER_CONFIG,
        code_version="headline-joint-bvar6-sensitivity-v1",
    )

    comparison = lag_comparison_table(
        {
            6: result_6,
            12: result_12,
        }
    )
    display(comparison)

    forecast_6 = forecast_headline_joint_bvar(
        result_6,
        native_levels=native_levels,
        H=FORECAST_HORIZON,
        n_draws=min(FORECAST_DRAWS, result_6["n_draws"]),
        simulate_future_outliers=True,
        seed=2026,
    )
    headline_forecast_6 = aggregate_headline_draws(
        forecast_6,
        native_levels=native_levels,
        weights=weights,
        official_total=official_total,
    )

    print("BVAR(6) Headline YoY")
    display(headline_forecast_table(headline_forecast_6, kind="yoy"))
else:
    print(
        "BVAR(6) sensitivity disabled. Set RUN_BVAR6_SENSITIVITY=True "
        "only after the canonical BVAR(12) run is validated."
    )

Current production contract¶

Excel / Haver / Eurostat
        │
        ├─ HICP Energy
        ├─ HICP Food      (H023HA1@EUDATA)
        ├─ HICP NEIG
        └─ HICP Services
                ↓
       headline_joint_monthly.csv
                ↓
        all four → log state
                ↓
        dense joint BVAR(12)
        Minnesota + SV + outliers + DK
                ↓
      joint posterior component paths
                ↓
     annual HICP component weights
        Food weight = PF + UF
                ↓
       December-rebased chain linking
                ↓
          Headline HICP posterior
                ↓
              dashboard

Deferred decomposition models remain separate:

notebooks/decomposition/
    11 Unprocessed Food
    12 Processed Food
    13 NEIG
    14 Services

They are not required by the current joint Headline production pipeline.
